purpose: Define the types and trait every language analyzer builds on -- LanguageId, CapabilityPrecision, AnalyzerCapabilities, AnalysisProfile, LanguageAnalyzer and FileAnalysis -- per docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md Sections 11 and 13, with the corrections in docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md section 20. FileAnalysis is a core type and is not Serialize (05 section 19).
scope: crates/monokl/src/analysis/{mod,lang,file_analysis}.rs. No implementations of the trait, no registry, no NodeKind (oxc-dependent; ships with the TypeScript analyzer).
non_goals: Any LanguageAnalyzer implementation and the AnalyzerRegistry.

What an analyzer does when analyze_with_profile receives a path supports() rejects, and what capabilities() returns for a language not in languages(). The registry only calls analyzers after supports(); the registry and analyzer tracks decide.

Persisting FileAnalysis. Track 17 defines persist::v1 types and owes a round-trip criterion: converting a FileAnalysis to its persisted form and back preserves source_path, digest, profile, had_parse_errors and language().

api_surface.name: LanguageId
api_surface.signature: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)] pub enum LanguageId { TypeScript, Rust, Python, Go, Java, C, Cpp, Bash, CSharp, Ruby, Php, Kotlin, Scala }
api_surface.description: Part 1 section 11's 13 variants in its order, plus PartialOrd and Ord (05 section 20).

api_surface.name: CapabilityPrecision
api_surface.signature: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)] pub enum CapabilityPrecision { Unsupported, Heuristic, Structural, Exact }
api_surface.description: Weakest to strongest, so gating compares with <.

api_surface.name: AnalyzerCapabilities
api_surface.signature: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct AnalyzerCapabilities { pub blocks: bool, pub classified_imports: bool, pub resolved_import_graph: CapabilityPrecision, pub refs: CapabilityPrecision, pub definition: CapabilityPrecision, pub inspect_detail: CapabilityPrecision }
api_surface.description: What one analyzer can do for one language.

api_surface.name: AnalysisProfile
api_surface.signature: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum AnalysisProfile { Dependencies, Structural, Full }
api_surface.description: How much to extract. Dependencies fills dependencies only; Structural adds symbols and exports; Full adds blocks and the per-language entries.

api_surface.name: LanguageAnalyzer
api_surface.signature: pub trait LanguageAnalyzer: Send + Sync { fn languages(&self) -> &[LanguageId]; fn supports(&self, path: &Utf8Path) -> bool; fn language_for(&self, path: &Utf8Path) -> Option<LanguageId>; fn capabilities(&self, language: LanguageId) -> AnalyzerCapabilities; fn analyze_with_profile(&self, path: &Utf8Path, source: Box<dyn FnOnce() -> Result<String>>, profile: AnalysisProfile) -> Result<Arc<FileAnalysis>>; fn analyze(&self, path: &Utf8Path, source: Box<dyn FnOnce() -> Result<String>>) -> Result<Arc<FileAnalysis>> { self.analyze_with_profile(path, source, AnalysisProfile::Full) } }
api_surface.description: Part 1 section 11 verbatim. language_for is None exactly when supports is false.

api_surface.name: FileAnalysis
api_surface.signature: #[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct FileAnalysis { pub source_path: Utf8PathBuf, pub digest: Digest, pub profile: AnalysisProfile, pub had_parse_errors: bool, pub symbols: Vec<SymbolEntry>, pub dependencies: Vec<DependencyRecord>, pub exports: Vec<ExportRecord>, pub blocks: Vec<CodeBlock>, pub lang: LangData }
api_surface.description: Everything extracted from one file, owned, no lifetimes, no serde. Under Dependencies, symbols, exports and blocks are empty; under Structural, blocks is empty.

api_surface.name: FileAnalysis::language, is_typescript, jsx_elements
api_surface.signature: pub fn language(&self) -> &str; pub fn is_typescript(&self) -> bool; pub fn jsx_elements(&self) -> &[JsxElementEntry]
api_surface.description: As Part 1 section 13: language is "typescript", "rust", "python", "go" or "java" by LangData variant; jsx_elements delegates to LangData::jsx_elements.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: LanguageId's 13 variants are in the declared order, so each is less than the next (checked pairwise over the whole list), and a BTreeSet built by inserting Scala, TypeScript, Rust, Go iterates as TypeScript, Rust, Go, Scala. It is Copy and works as a HashMap key.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Ord is the compile fix recorded in 05 section 20.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: CapabilityPrecision orders Unsupported < Heuristic < Structural < Exact.
AnalyzerCapabilities is Copy and equal to another value only if all six fields are equal: changing any one field of a value makes it unequal to the original.

analyze calls analyze_with_profile with AnalysisProfile::Full, passes the path and source closure through unchanged without calling the closure itself, and returns its result unchanged: a test analyzer that records its arguments records Full and the given path; its Err(MonoklError::TooManyTerms { count: 1, limit: 1 }) comes back as that error, and its Ok(arc) comes back as the same Arc (Arc::ptr_eq).
LanguageAnalyzer works as Arc<dyn LanguageAnalyzer> shared across threads: an Arc built from a test analyzer is moved into a spawned thread and calls languages() there.

FileAnalysis::language returns "typescript", "rust", "python", "go" and "java" for LangData::Ts, Rust, Python, Go and Java; is_typescript is true only for Ts; jsx_elements returns the TsData's two elements in order for Ts and an empty slice for the other four.

FileAnalysis is owned and thread-shareable: a function requiring Clone + Debug + Send + Sync + 'static accepts it. A clone has the same source_path, digest, profile, had_parse_errors and Debug text as the original. digest is a crate::digest::Digest and profile is an AnalysisProfile.
